# Runtime Data Ledger rev 2 - group codec-tools

Part of the [runtime data ledger, rev 2](../RUNTIME-DATA-LEDGER.md) (the index: vocabularies, totals, entity model, kernel features, decisions). **Tree:** `D:/wt/joltab`, `merge/ke16-into-ecsnative` @ `d11962a9`. **Rows:** 527, of which **527 active**; 285 non_rows (kept in the group JSON ledger).

Active forms: out-of-scope:compile-time 471, system-scratch 38, resource-column 15, out-of-scope:os-owned 2, diagnostics 1. Active classes: B 50, X 3, D 1, T 2, C 471. Crates: boyko_fontbake 44, boyko_image 18, boyko_serialize 30, boyko_shaderdsl 420, prof_decode 15. Rungs: OOS 473, R6 54.

## Findings

- Gate binaries that install DenyAfterSteady would abort inside std's path conversion on any save or load after `enter_steady()` (rows save.rs:717 and load.rs:312, class T). This stays true even after every other serialize row moves, unless file I/O goes through our own CreateFileW FFI.
- load.rs:579 uses a stable sort, which allocates scratch space when len > 20. sort_unstable_by_key removes that.

## Primitives refuted

- **VmBytes (public VmReservation-backed growable u8 buffer; new_primitives[0])**
  - replaced by: resource-column for the pixel payloads (DecodedImage::pixels, unfilter/expand outputs, AtlasImage::pixels, read_bfont's texel copy): a byte payload lane of the per-type staging Resource via KF-loader-decode-context, the form the render group gave TextureData.rgba8; system-scratch for the save image, the save_world_to_file buffer and the loaded file bytes: a ScratchColumn&lt;u8> in the save/load system's state via KF-serialize-seam-on-kernel-columns.
  - evidence: Every VmBytes user is a handoff or a call transient, not a new kind of storage: pixels are consumed by boyko_render/src/gpu_upload.rs:114 "for staged in staging.drain() {" or boyko_render/src/ui/resources.rs:458 "let pixels = &font.atlas.pixels;"; the save image by boyko_serialize/src/save.rs:717 "std::fs::write(path, &buf)?;".; The byte storage already exists as a kernel column: a ComponentPool of stride 1 (boyko_ecs/src/ecs/memory/component_pool.rs:334 "let stride = component_layout.size();") that grows in place (boyko_ecs/src/ecs/core/component/scratch/scratch_column.rs:33 "`ComponentPool` grows IN PLACE").; boyko_image needs no buffer type at all: the final size is known before the first pixel write (boyko_image/src/png.rs:131 "let final_size = (info.width as usize)"), so it writes a caller slice - consistent with boyko_image/Cargo.toml:5 "it takes no other workspace crate."; The same proposal appears in the allocator design as a Column-class primitive (D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:142 "pub type ByteColumn = VmColumn&lt;MaybeUninit&lt;u8>>;"); recorded as a plan conflict, not silently overridden.
- **CallScratch / ScratchVec&lt;T> (call-scoped VmReservation bump arena handing out typed growable vectors; new_primitives[1])**
  - replaced by: system-scratch: one ScratchColumn&lt;T> per array, owned by the state of the system that runs the call (the asset loader's decode context for boyko_image; the save/load exclusive system for boyko_serialize), kept at its high-water mark; nested Vecs flattened to sibling columns plus (start,len); LoadColumn de-lifetimed by KF-serialize-seam-on-kernel-columns; ids minted by the existing register_asset_layout.
  - evidence: The ECS already has per-system state: boyko_ecs/src/ecs/core/system/params/local.rs:62 "pub struct Local&lt;'s, T: Send + Sync + Default + 'static>(pub(crate) &'s mut T);" for function systems, and the closure state of boyko_ecs/src/ecs/core/system/exclusive_function_system.rs:1 "`System` adapter for `fn(&mut EcsMaster)`." for exclusive ones.; The one reason given for a new arena - growth without relocation - is what ScratchColumn already does (boyko_ecs/src/ecs/core/component/scratch/scratch_column.rs:33 "`ComponentPool` grows IN PLACE"). Only the ViaFn byte runs (save.rs:74/207, dense ViaFn data) grow to a size unknown before encoding; every other length is known before its first write, and the serialization plan already allows removing even those with a sizing pass (D:/wt/joltab/docs/SERIALIZATION-PLAN.md:328 "owning = run each `serialize_fn` against a sizing sink").; The DEFLATE side needs neither growth nor an arena: the zlib output is exact (boyko_image/src/inflate.rs:674 "let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(expected_len);") and the Huffman subtable is bounded (boyko_image/src/inflate.rs:282 "let sub_len = (1usize &lt;&lt; ROOT_BITS) &lt;&lt; self.sub_bits;" with ROOT_BITS = 9, MAX_CODE_BITS = 15); LZ77 read-back of its own prefix is an index into a slice.; A kernel type-keyed column mint already exists and is used outside assets: boyko_ecs/src/ecs/core/asset/backing.rs:115 "pub fn register_asset_layout&lt;T: 'static>(drop_fn: Option&lt;DropFn>) -> ComponentId {"; boyko_render/src/particle_system.rs:16 "(`register_asset_layout::<T>(None)` + [`pool_reserve_rows`]), never `std::Vec`.".; Residual cost, stated rather than hidden: each ScratchColumn is its own reservation with a commit granule of boyko_ecs/src/ecs/constants.rs:7 "pub const COMMIT_GRANULE: usize = 64 * 1024;", so a dozen save/load scratch columns keep more resident memory than one bump arena while the system state lives. On a cold command that is acceptable, and dropping the columns after the command is equally legal; if it is not acceptable, the answer is the kernel's packing plan or the frame/scope arenas the F and S classes need anyway - not a codec-only arena.
- **VmColumn domain extension for element sizes that do not divide COMMIT_GRANULE (GlyphMetrics = 36 B; new_primitives[2])**
  - replaced by: resource-column on ComponentPool, owned by the boyko_ui FontTable Resource (the durable home), with read_bfont parsing straight into it through a generic sink.
  - evidence: boyko_ecs/src/ecs/memory/component_pool.rs:334 "let stride = component_layout.size();" - ComponentPool has no divisibility pin, unlike boyko_ecs/src/ecs/memory/vm_column.rs:145 "COMMIT_GRANULE.is_multiple_of(Self::SIZE),".; Precedent for a Resource-owned ComponentPool table of non-component rows: boyko_ecs/src/ecs/core/asset/assets.rs:201 "col: ComponentPool,", with its layout minted by boyko_ecs/src/ecs/core/asset/backing.rs:115 "pub fn register_asset_layout&lt;T: 'static>(drop_fn: Option&lt;DropFn>) -> ComponentId {".; Independently, the allocator design plans to drop the VmColumn pin for every size (D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:123 "`VmColumn::new` drops the `COMMIT_GRANULE % size_of::<T>() == 0` pin"), so no bespoke primitive survives on either route.; The BakedFont Vecs are a load intermediate that FontEntry::from_baked clones (boyko_ui/src/text/font.rs:72 "glyphs: font.glyphs.clone().into_boxed_slice(),"); the datum's ECS home is boyko_ui/src/text/font.rs:139 "fonts: Vec&lt;FontEntry>," (a ui-group row).

## Plan conflicts

- D:/wt/joltab/docs/ARCH-AUDIT-ECS-DATA-REMEDIATION.md:9 "boyko_serialize (function-local I/O scratch);" lists boyko_serialize's function-local I/O scratch as LEGIT (exempt), in line with CLAUDE.md:18 "truly transient function-local scratch." The owner's 2026-09-10 order ('move ALL runtime data structures onto our system') and this ledger put those 30 serialize rows (25 B + 3 X + 2 T; the 2 T rows cannot move) on kernel scratch columns (system-scratch). The order and the audit disagree and the CLAUDE.md exception text still stands; not resolved silently.
- D:/wt/joltab/docs/SERIALIZATION-PLAN.md:285 "Concrete monomorphic `SaveCursor<'a>` (append-only over a preallocated `Vec<u8>`," and D:/wt/joltab/docs/SERIALIZATION-PLAN.md:313 "pub fn save_world(world: &EcsMaster, opts: &SaveOptions, out: &mut Vec&lt;u8>) -> Result&lt;usize, SaveError>;" fix the save output as a Vec&lt;u8>. This ledger routes the image to a ScratchColumn&lt;u8> and needs the cursor reshaped (KF-serialize-seam-on-kernel-columns). The plan predates the 2026-09-10 order.
- D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:50 "\| `offline` \| `boyko_macros` (proc-macro), `aether_lang`, `boyko_shaderdsl` printer, `boyko_fontbake` \| compile/bake time \| not in the runtime binary or run once at bake \|" tags all of boyko_fontbake as offline. But read_bfont and BakedFont are the declared runtime load path (boyko_ui/Cargo.toml:25, boyko_render/Cargo.toml:59; re-exported by boyko_ui/src/text/mod.rs:51), so those 8 rows stay class B with ECS forms. The offline tag is right for the 36 baker rows. Note: no non-test code calls read_bfont today.
- D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:361 "`prefab.rs`, `serialize/mod.rs:288`, `load_writer.rs`, `mesh_data.rs`, `texture_data.rs`," (rung 4) sends texture_data.rs - where the 8-bit boyko_image pixels end up - and the kernel serialize siblings to HeapVec, a relocating heap beside ComponentPool (D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:114 "**no** (relocates on grow)") whose back-pointer design the critique holds as blocking UB (D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:460 "**Heap back-pointer aliasing is UB under Tree Borrows as designed.**"). This ledger sends the pixel rows to resource-column lanes and the serialize rows to system-scratch, both on ComponentPool-backed columns. The boyko_serialize rows themselves are not named in rung 4.
- D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:111 "`ScratchColumn` + new `DropColumn<T>`, `ByteColumn`" / D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:142 "pub type ByteColumn = VmColumn&lt;MaybeUninit&lt;u8>>;" propose ByteColumn, a VmColumn-based byte primitive beside ComponentPool. It is the same need as the inventory's VmBytes; this ledger refutes both with ScratchColumn&lt;u8> (ComponentPool-backed). Same need, different home.
- D:/claude/BoykoEngine/docs/memory/ALLOCATOR-DESIGN-SPACE.md:341 "`Staging.queue` \| `VmColumn` stacks" sends the staging queue to VmColumn stacks, but Staged&lt;A> carries a non-Copy Cpu payload (boyko_render/src/texture_data.rs:28 'pub rgba8: Vec&lt;u8>,', the render group's row) while boyko_ecs/src/ecs/memory/vm_column.rs:80 "pub(crate) struct VmColumn&lt;T: Copy> {" is Copy-only. The queue becomes a Copy column only once the payload moves out of line, which is KF-loader-decode-context. The staging row belongs to the ecs-services group, whose verified destination is a third one (NEW:VmQueue&lt;T>, already refuted by the render group); recorded here because these payload rows decide it.
- Within the ledger: the recount wrote Resource+VmColumn for atlas.rs:128/130/611/619 and a VmColumn domain extension for atlas.rs:126/598; the ui group's verified rows propose NEW:CsrColumn&lt;GlyphMetrics / MappedCodepoint / KernPair> for the FontEntry tables (boyko_ui/src/text/font.rs:33/38/41/72/75) that hold the same datum. This ledger's form for the fontbake rows is resource-column on ComponentPool (flat FontTable columns plus (start,len) per font, i.e. CSR on existing storage). The ui rows are the ui ecsform analyst's to decide; flagged so the two do not diverge.

[rev2 GAP 6] ecs_form diagnostics (new explicit form, decided by performance): cold diagnostic text and error payloads, built only on error / report paths, so the cost that matters is I-cache and the emitting thread's time, not allocation speed. Home, chosen per site: a &'static str or structured code (no bytes at all), a boyko_log ring record with formatting deferred to the drain (off the emitting thread), or a cold VmReservation-backed byte arena for a payload that must outlive the call; the recount's memory destination (DspBuf / InlineStr / DiagArena / KF-10 structured error) names which. Not kernel-internal: it is not the kernel's storage bookkeeping (most of these rows are in boyko_app and boyko_render), and moving it out lets the gate on kernel-internal close. Not out of scope: our code allocates it. Class: #[cold] #[inline(never)] diagnostic on a CRC-32 mismatch (load time, RatePolicy::Every). String::from_utf8_lossy returns Cow&lt;str>: it allocates ONLY when the 4 bytes are not valid UTF-8; chunk types are ASCII by spec, so the heap arm is reached only for a corrupt chunk type. Until that rung lands, this row stays out of scope and the deny gate must not be armed around save or load.
